column1: Because the central bank must respond to partial and incomplete information about the true state of the economy, monetary policy is often formulated in practice in terms of intermediate targets. Intermediate targets are variables whose behavior provides information useful in forecasting the goal variables. Deviations in the intermediate targets from their expected paths indicate a likely deviation of a goal variable from its target and signal the need for a policy adjustment. For example, if money growth, which is observed weekly, is closely related to subsequent inflation, which is observed only monthly, then faster than expected money growth signals the need to tighten policy. When action is taken to keep the intermediate target variable equal to its target, the hope is that policy will be adjusted automatically to keep the goal variables close to their targets as well.
